blunderbuss: short gun with a wide, flared barrel, used at close range
mantilla: lace or silk veil worn over the head and shoulders
castanets: small wooden clappers clicked together by the fingers while dancing
guard-room: room where soldiers on guard duty wait and rest
piastre: silver coin used in Spain and other countries at the time
ducats: gold coins once used in Spain and Italy
doubloon: old Spanish gold coin of high value
guineas: old British gold coins worth one pound and one shilling
gallows: wooden frame on which criminals were hanged to death
venta: roadside inn in Spain where travellers stopped
picador: mounted bullfighter who weakens the bull with a lance
priming-pin: pin used to ignite the powder in an old firearm
repeater: gun or watch that can fire or strike several times
gipsydom: the world, customs, or community of gipsies
gitana: Spanish word for a gipsy woman
brigand: bandit who robs travellers, often living in the mountains
orregidor: Spanish chief magistrate or local governor of a town
presidio: fortress or prison used for convicts in Spanish colonies
galleys: long rowing ships, or punishment of rowing them as convicts
leagues: old units of distance, roughly three miles each
paces: steps taken while walking, used as a measure of distance
brushwood: small broken branches and undergrowth in woods
yemas: sweets made from sugar and egg yolks
sugar-plums: small sweets made of sugar, often with a nut or seed inside
sward: surface of short green grass or turf
astern: at or toward the back end of a ship
beheld: saw or looked upon, an old-fashioned word
neighed: made the loud cry of a horse
thorough-paced: fully trained, skilled, and complete in every way
togged: dressed up smartly in fine clothes
dragoons: cavalry soldiers who could fight on horseback or on foot
lancers: cavalry soldiers armed with long spears
loadstone: magnetic stone, another name for lodestone
wallet: small leather bag or pouch for carrying money
sulky: sullen, moody, and unwilling to speak or cooperate
fatigue: military duty such as manual labour assigned to soldiers
posted: stationed at a particular place for duty
quits: even, with no debt or grudge remaining between people
afresh: again, starting over from the beginning
vengeance: punishment or harm done in return for a wrong
remorse: deep regret for a wrong one has done
hermitage: dwelling place of a religious hermit, living alone
queer: strange or odd, in an old-fashioned sense
spark: lively young man, or a lover, in old-fashioned speech
ruffian: violent, lawless man who attacks or bullies others
countenance: face, or the expression on someone's face
nomads: wandering people who move from place to place
sorceress: woman believed to practise magic or witchcraft
witchcraft: magic practised by witches, using supernatural powers
spells: magic words or actions meant to cast a charm
superstitions: beliefs based on fear or magic rather than reason
sloe: small wild plum with a sour, bitter taste
mantilla's: lace or silk veil worn over the head and shoulders
